correctness.rationale: Direct subgroup support conversion by lcm is bijective; the degree formula and its unique minimum-degree layer follow by a strict neighbor inclusion. An undeleted singleton clique survives any deletion of at most 2^t-1 vertices because r>=2^t. Every vertex outside its component contains all surviving singleton indices, so such vertices are mutually nonadjacent and must be isolated. Isolation needs its full neighborhood deleted, proving the complete cut characterization. Whitney inequalities yield edge connectivity. All assumptions and boundaries checked, direct finite verification covers 32,519 deletion cases; finite tests are not used to prove the universal statement.

originality.rationale: The 2026 motivating primary paper proves only 2-connectivity for the t=2 graph, not exact 3-connectivity or minimum-cut enumeration, and does not treat the t-filtration. Rather 2026 treats a weighted graph on ring elements with all support levels, while this theorem treats one vertex per subgroup and truncates support. Prior uniform-layer Kneser super-connectivity does not imply these nonuniform filtered graphs without further argument. No equivalent statement was found in the actual queries; residual risk of other terminology remains.

value.rationale: The recent paper establishes 2-connectivity for the pendant-free graph but gives no exact vertex resilience. This result provides an exact exponential robustness law through the natural prime-support filtration, identifies every optimal destructive subgroup set, counts the cuts binomial(r,t), and proves exactly which subgroup becomes isolated. This is a structural and complete infinite-family classification, not a small isolated numerical improvement.
